cards.explanation: The answer is cross. Simon of Cyrene, a man coming in from the country, gets the cross put on him to carry behind Jesus. Luke says the soldiers seized him. I think Simon woke up that morning with a totally different to-do list. Some days just grab you by the collar, friends.

The answer is themselves and their children. Jesus turns to these women, the daughters of Jerusalem, and says, “…do not weep for Me, but weep for yourselves and for your children.” Think about that, friends. He's on His way to the cross, and He's still the one looking out for them. Then He goes on to warn them about days that are coming. He sure doesn't brush them off.

The answer is blessed. Jesus says, “Blessed are the barren women, the wombs that never bore, and breasts that never nursed!” That's what people will say in the days He warns about. It's a strange thing to hear, and I think it tells us how heavy those days will be. He goes on to say people will call on the mountains and hills to fall on them and cover them.

The answer is False. Luke calls them criminals, not disciples. He says, “Two others, who were criminals, were also led away to be executed with Jesus.” So Jesus isn't the only one led away. And hold onto those two, friends, because one of them ends up in a conversation you won't forget.

The answer is one on His right and the other on His left. At The Skull, they crucified Jesus “…along with the criminals, one on His right and the other on His left.” So He has one criminal on each side. Luke doesn't tell us anything more about how they were arranged, so I won't add details. Remember those two, friends, because they're about to matter.

The answer is that He asks the Father to forgive them because they don't know what they're doing. Jesus says, “Father, forgive them, for they do not know what they are doing.” Look at where He is when He says it, friends. He's hanging on a cross, and He prays for forgiveness. I think that's one of the most powerful lines in the whole passage.
The answer is True. Luke says they divided up His garments by casting lots. That's a way of settling who gets what. It happens right after Jesus prays for them to be forgiven.

The answer is that the soldiers say, “If You are the King of the Jews, save Yourself!” Sound familiar, friends? The rulers sneered something close to it just a verse or two before. Same kind of taunt, and now it's coming from the soldiers too.

The answer is whether he even fears God. The second criminal says, “Do you not even fear God, since you are under the same judgment?” Look at that, friends. He's hanging on a cross himself, and he still stops to correct the other man. I think a lot is changing in his heart right here.

The answer is True. The second criminal says, “We are punished justly, for we are receiving what our actions deserve.” Notice he says we, so he's including himself. That takes honesty, especially on a day like that. Then he turns and speaks up for Jesus.

The answer is wrong. The second criminal says, “But this man has done nothing wrong.” He's just admitted that he and the other man deserve what they're getting. Then he turns around and says that about Jesus. It's a clear line between them, friends.

The answer is Paradise. Jesus tells the criminal, “Truly I tell you, today you will be with Me in Paradise.” Hold on to the word today, friends. The man asked to be remembered, and Jesus answers with a promise. I think that man heard more than he ever hoped to.

The answer is that the veil is torn down the middle. Luke says the veil of the temple was torn down the middle. He puts it in the same verse as the sun being darkened. Luke doesn't explain what it means in this passage, so I won't guess. I'll just say it's a big moment, friends.

The answer is “Father, into Your hands I commit My Spirit.” Jesus calls out those words in a loud voice. Even now, friends, He's talking to His Father. Then Luke says He breathed His last. I think this one deserves a quiet moment.

The answer is True. Luke says the centurion saw what happened and “…gave glory to God…” He's a Roman army officer, and he's standing at a crucifixion. Then he says, “Surely this was a righteous man.” I think that's a real surprise, friends.

The answer is righteous. The centurion, a Roman army officer, says, “Surely this was a righteous man.” He's standing right there at the crucifixion, saying it out loud. One of the criminals hanging beside Jesus had already said, “But this man has done nothing wrong.” Two different men, friends, same kind of statement.

The answer is False. The crowd doesn't head home cheering. Luke says that when the people who had gathered saw what happened, “…they returned home beating their breasts.” I think it shows they walked home shaken, friends. Luke doesn't say more about what was going through their minds.

The answer is that they're standing at a distance watching. Luke says all those who knew Jesus, including the women who had followed Him from Galilee, “…stood at a distance watching these things.” They didn't leave, friends. They stayed and watched. I think that says a lot about them.
